scenario.name: AWS EKS Security, Unit 42 & MITRE — Amazon EKS aws-auth ConfigMap system:masters RBAC Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud-managed Kubernetes complex whose front reception desk translates AWS corporate badges into inner building keys using one hand-edited paper seating chart taped behind the desk. Using a pre-signed AWS badge to sign in, an intruder edits that single paper seating chart to write their own ordinary cloud role straight into the Supreme Master Guild line, instantly unlocking every secret vault in the entire cluster. In this scenario (T1078.004, AWS EKS Security, Unit 42 & MITRE, Amazon EKS aws-auth ConfigMap system:masters RBAC Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: eKS STS Presigned Bearer Token, then patching kube-system/aws-auth mapUsers /, then cluster-Admin Secret Enumeration. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering EKS STS Presigned Bearer Token, then Patching kube-system/aws-auth mapUsers /, then Cluster-Admin Secret Enumeration, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: EKS STS Presigned Bearer Token Authentication (k8s-aws-v1.<base64>)
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1078.004 - Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: Generating a short-lived pre-signed AWS identity voucher wrapped inside a special cluster prefix, the intruder presents it to the Kubernetes front gate to authenticate smoothly with an existing cloud IAM badge. An AWS IAM principal authenticates to the Amazon EKS API server by generating a presigned STS GetCallerIdentity URL encoded as a Bearer token (k8s-aws-v1.<base64>), which aws-iam-authenticator maps to Kubernetes groups via kube-system/aws-auth (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EksClusterAuth=aws-iam-authenticator , k8s-aws-v1 token, CallerIamArn=arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/eks-ci-deployer/build-01, TargetConfigMap=kube-system/aws-auth so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes aws eks get-token --cluster-name prod-eks-cluster (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws eks get-token --cluster-name prod-eks-cluster against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audit, or so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1078.004 during "EKS STS Presigned Bearer Token Authentication , k8s-aws-v1.<base64>" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl get configmap aws-auth -n kube-system -o yaml runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get configmap aws-auth -n kube-system -o yaml configuring pod security con so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1078.004 during "EKS STS Presigned Bearer Token Authentication , k8s-aws-v1.<base64>" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ GET /api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/configmaps/aws-auth / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 Compromised CI/CD IAM Role) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 system:masters ClusterAdmin Access).

stages.title: Stage 2: Patching kube-system/aws-auth mapUsers / mapRoles with system:masters Group
stages.subtitle: Persistence & Privilege Escalation (T1098 - Account Manipulation)
stages.description: Opening the delicate translation chart taped inside the system room, the intruder appends a second backdoor cloud user directly underneath the unrestrictable Supreme Master Guild, granting permanent cluster-wide sovereignty that survives even RBAC cleanups. Using update/patch permissions on ConfigMaps in kube-system, the actor appends a secondary IAM role or user ARN into data.mapUsers with groups: ["system:masters"], granting persistent cluster-admin authority that bypasses Kubernetes RoleBindings (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditVerb=patch , kube-system/aws-auth, InjectedMapping=rolearn: readonly-audit-role -> groups: [system:masters], PrivilegeLevel=Built-in Kubernetes Superuser , system:masters so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes fields @timestamp, user.username, objectRef.name, requestObject.data.mapUsers | filter objectRef.name == "aws-auth" and verb in ["update", "patch"] (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , fields @timestamp, user.username, objectRef.name, requestObject.data.mapUsers | filter objec so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1098 during "Patching kube-system/aws-auth mapUsers / mapRoles with system:masters Group" , Using update/patch permissions on ConfigMaps in kube-system, the actor appends a secondary IAM role or user ARN into data while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl describe configmap aws-auth -n kube-system runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl describe configmap aws-auth -n kube-system configuring pod security contex so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1098 during "Patching kube-system/aws-auth mapUsers / mapRoles with system:masters Group" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/configmaps/aws-auth (mapRoles -> system:masters) / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Amazon EKS Control Plane API), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 system:masters ClusterAdmin Access).

stages.title: Stage 3: Cluster-Admin Secret Enumeration & EKS Access Entry Remediation
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.007 - Container API)
stages.description: Now holding Supreme Master Guild status across the entire cluster, the intruder reads every application secret in every namespace until security engineers migrate the cluster off the fragile paper chart onto managed, auditable cloud access entries. Authenticating as the newly mapped IAM role, the actor inherits system:masters group membership (which is hardcoded into kube-apiserver to bypass RBAC authorization checks) and lists cluster secrets (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EffectiveGroup=system:masters, AuthzDecision=allow , Built-in Superuser Group, TargetResource=/api/v1/secrets so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes aws eks update-cluster-config --name prod-eks-cluster --access-config authenticationMode=API (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws eks update-cluster-config --name prod-eks-cluster --access-config authenticationMode=API so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.007 during "Cluster-Admin Secret Enumeration & EKS Access Entry Remediation" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact aws eks list-access-entries --cluster-name prod-eks-cluster runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws eks list-access-entries --cluster-name prod-eks-cluster against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.007 during "Cluster-Admin Secret Enumeration & EKS Access Entry Remediation" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ LIST /api/v1/secrets as group system:masters / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Amazon EKS Control Plane API) to Node ④ (#4 kube-system/aws-auth ConfigMap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 system:masters ClusterAdmin Access).

keySpecs.value: Switch the EKS cluster to authenticationMode=API (disabling the aws-auth ConfigMap completely) and audit all EKS Access Entries via AWS CloudTrail.
